marks.gloss_en: דאמר רבי אלעזר: למי נאה למלל גבורות ה' -- למי שיכול להשמיע כל תהלתו (kind svara: no support kind names an amoraic dictum adduced with דאמר)
from here on it is forbidden to recount the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He
וכי מאחר דמאה ועשרים זקנים ומהם כמה נביאים תקנו תפלה על הסדר, שמעון הפקולי מאי הסדיר?
שכחום, וחזר וסדרום -- they were forgotten, and he arranged them again
אימא קודם עבודה? -- say [birkat kohanim] before the avoda [blessing]! (Steinsaltz: the verse seems to have Aaron bless and then go down to sacrifice)
לא סלקא דעתך, דכתיב וירד מעשת החטאת -- מי כתיב לעשות? מעשות כתיב: he came down FROM offering
ולימרה אחר העבודה! -- then say it immediately after the avoda blessing
לא סלקא דעתך, דכתיב זובח תודה (= p_hodaah_achar_avoda)
מאי חזית דסמכת אהאי, סמוך אהאי! -- what did you see to rely on this [verse]? rely on that one! (Steinsaltz: why let Ps 50:23 place hodaah after avoda rather than Lev 9:22 place birkat kohanim there)
מסתברא: עבודה והודאה חדא מילתא היא -- it stands to reason: service and thanksgiving are one matter
once David comes, prayer comes: 'I will bring them to My holy mountain and gladden them in My house of prayer' (Isa 56:7)
once prayer comes, the [Temple] service comes: 'their burnt-offerings and sacrifices shall be accepted on My altar' (Isa 56:7)
birkat kohanim after hodaah: 'and Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them, and came down from offering the sin-offering, the burnt-offering and the peace-offerings' (Lev 9:22)

sim shalom after birkat kohanim: 'and they shall place My name upon the children of Israel and I will bless them' (Num 6:27); the Holy One's blessing is peace -- 'the Lord will bless His people with peace' (Ps 29:11)
R' Yochanan: one who recounts the praise of the Holy One excessively is uprooted from the world -- 'shall it be told Him when I speak? if a man says it, he is swallowed up' (Job 37:20)
R' Yehuda of Kfar Gibboraya: 'to You silence is praise' (Ps 65:2) -- the remedy of all is silence
אתיא זכירה זכירה: כתיב הכא והימים האלה נזכרים, וכתיב התם כתב זאת זכרון בספר -- as there in a book, so here in a book
מנלן? -- the Megilla's remembrance is in a book (gezera shava זכירה-זכירה), so reading by heart does not fulfil the obligation
Rava: the remembrance of the Megilla ('these days are remembered', Esther 9:28) must be in a book, as the remembrance of Amalek ('write this as a remembrance in the book', Ex 17:14)
the baraita: 'remember' is with the mouth, not the heart -- so the remembrance is reading aloud, not mere looking
וממאי דהאי זכירה קריאה היא, דלמא עיון בעלמא -- perhaps the remembrance 'in the book' is mere looking into it, not reading
לא סלקא דעתך: the baraita -- 'remember' cannot be in the heart, since 'you shall not forget' already covers the heart; so 'remember' is with the mouth (= p_zachor_bapeh)
this remembrance [in the book] is reading, not mere looking
(entertained) the clause speaks of a Megilla written in the original and read in translation
והא אמרת: קראה בכל לשון לא יצא! -- the mishnah itself says that reading in any other language does not fulfil the obligation
רב ושמואל דאמרי תרוייהו: בלעז יווני -- the foreign language the mishnah permits is Greek (= p_laaz_yevani)
Rav and Shmuel: the foreign language of the mishnah's לועזות clause is Greek
אטו אנן ... מי ידעינן? אלא ... הכא נמי -- what holds for us, who do not know those words, holds here too
מתקיף לה רבינא: אטו אנן האחשתרנים בני הרמכים מי ידעינן? -- even we do not understand every word, so understanding cannot be the requirement
Ravina: do even we know [the meaning of] 'ha'achashteranim benei haramakhim' (Esther 8:10)?
והא לא ידע מאי קאמרי? -- but he does not understand what they are saying!
מידי דהוה אנשים ועמי הארץ -- just as women and the unlearned fulfil it (= p_dami_nashim_veamei_haaretz)
the premise of the stam's question: one who does not understand what is being said does not fulfil the obligation
seirugin is [entering, or reading] in separate portions -- the narrator's 'piskei piskei' for what the maidservant called 'seirugin seirugin'
חלוגלוגות is what the man was scattering, פרפחיני (purslane, per Steinsaltz) -- as Rebbi's maidservant called it
סלסלה (Prov 4:8) is the word for turning over, as the maidservant said to a man turning his hair over: how long will you מסלסל your hair?
יהבך (Ps 55:23) is a load (טונא): Rabba bar bar Chana, carrying a load, was told by an Arab: take your יהב and throw it on my camel
מטאטא (Isa 14:23) is the טאטיתא with which one טאטי's a house, as the maidservant told her friend (a broom and sweeping, per Steinsaltz)
one who read it at intervals has fulfilled his obligation
דתנן, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר: אף ספרים לא התירו שיכתבו אלא יוונית -- kind svara: no SupportKind names a דתנן citation
והא קתני: יוונית ליוונים -- ליוונים אין, לכולי עלמא לא! -- the baraita implies Greek works only for Greeks
אינהו דאמור כרבן שמעון בן גמליאל -- Rav and Shmuel follow RSBG (= p_rav_ushmuel_kirsbg)
the stam's inference from the baraita: Greek to Greeks yes, to everyone no
מיתיבי: קראה גיפטית ... יוונית -- לא יצא! -- reading in Greek does not fulfil, against Rav and Shmuel's Greek
the baraita: one who read it in Coptic, Ivrit, Elamite, Median, Greek has not fulfilled his obligation
הא לא דמיא אלא להא -- the mishnah's clause matches the other baraita: each language to those who speak it (= p_matnitin_kebaraita)
the baraita: Coptic to Copts, Ivrit to Ivrim, Elamite to Elamites, Greek to Greeks -- he has fulfilled
אי הכי, רב ושמואל אמאי מוקמי לה למתניתין בלעז יווני? לוקמוה בכל לעז! -- if the mishnah means any language to its speakers, why restrict it to Greek?
[אלא מתניתין כברייתא,] וכי איתמר דרב ושמואל בעלמא איתמר: לעז יווני לכל כשר -- the memra was said independently, not on the mishnah (= p_yevani_lakol_kasher)
Rav and Shmuel, stated independently of the mishnah: the Greek language is valid for everyone
(entertained) the Greek case is a Megilla written in Ashurit and read in Greek
R' Elazar: the Holy One, Blessed be He, called Yaakov 'El'
(entertained) RSBG's Greek applies only to other books; for the Megilla, of which 'according to their writing' is written, not
